item.title: Canon Launches New Lenses and a Limited Edition Compact Camera
item.description: Not too long ago, there were reports of Canon introducing new wide-angle lenses. And early this morning, they finally launched the 14mm and 7-14mm lenses. However, there was also another surprise alongside this: a new limited edition G7X Mk III. Here is a look at the gear and how it is helpful.

item.title: Viltrox Launches L-Mount Support. Is Sony Doomed Now?
item.description: During the pandemic, I tested the first L-mount camera that really made me a convert: the Leica SL2s. And since then, I've switched my primary camera system to the L-mount -- which was then supported by Leica, Panasonic, and Sigma. Viltrox joined recently, and today, they're launching their first lens for the L-mount: the 16mm f1.8. What a lens to choose, considering that the camera system has nothing like it.

item.title: We Tested the Viltrox 16mm f1.8 for L-Mount and Found Something Crazy
item.description: Here at the Phoblographer, I've always encouraged our staff to really hold the manufacturers accountable to their statements. Viltrox has always stated that their 16mm f1.8 has weather resistance. Today, the company is announcing that it's coming to L-mount after being available for Nikon Z and Sony E mount. item.title: The Best Nikon Cameras for Street Photography
item.description: When it comes to street photography, there are various aspects that you need to get right with your cameras. For instance, a speedy autofocus, the ability to shoot in the dark, and a great form factor. With Nikon launching some interesting cameras, we take a look at a few options that have impressed us in various areas. Have a look.

item.title: The 3 DSLRs from 2016 That Still Deserve Respect in 2026
item.description: The DSLR technology began to actively fade right after the pandemic. The newer CIPA numbers from last year show that shipments have also dropped significantly. However, the truth remains that DSLRs continue to be important for many young photographers who need good cameras on a budget, such as full frames. If you are someone who is keen on buying a new camera, then here is a look at three options that can be ideal for various photographers.

item.title: Will Sony Develop a 28MP Micro Four Thirds Sensor?
item.description: Not too long ago, it was reported that Sony is set to launch a 180MP medium-format sensor, marking a leap in resolution and sensor technology. While the sensor is supposed to be part of a new generation of partially stacked sensor architecture, reports indicate that Sony is likely to introduce multiple sensor sizes of the same sensor. Here's how it can help MFT users.

item.title: The Godox AD100PROII Costs $300. But It Performs Like $1,000
item.description: Most flashes aren't just expensive, they're also really difficult to use for many of us who don't understand how to see light. That's one of the reasons why so many people reach for LEDs instead. But if flashes were more affordable and easy to use, more folks would pick them up. That's exactly why so many photographers have been reaching for Godox over the years. And with their new Godox AD100PROII, they're delivering a light that costs only $300 but performs far better.

item.title: Jeff Bezos Gave the Finger to Photographers. Help Us Give it Back
item.description: Ever since all the ethical hiring issues and lawsuits with B&H Photo, Amazon has been the Phoblographer's preferred retailer of choice when recommending to you folks where to buy camera gear from. Admittedly, I knew that I was trading one evil for another. But this week, Jeff Bezos crossed the line with laying off the entire photography staff of the Washington Post. We've been wanting to get rid of Amazon for a while -- and in order to do that, we need your help.

item.title: Sigma Quietly Discontinues Some of Its Most Beloved Lenses
item.description: Sigma has been one of the more popular third-party lens brands, and it's everyone's favorite. The company has offered a wide range of focal lengths, and it continues to add new offerings over time. It has now come to our attention that Sigma has quietly discontinued two prime lenses, which have been an ideal choice for street and landscape photographers.

item.title: Review: The Meike 85mm f1.8 Mark II is Great for Two Reasons
item.description: Not every portrait lens needs to be expensive to be effective. Sometimes all you need is visible sharpness, pleasing bokeh, and a price that doesn’t hurt your wallet. The Meike 85mm f1.8 Mark II is a prime (pun intended) example of such a lens.
